req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE (HEAD is implicit in Flask for GET routes, OPTIONS is handled by Flask automatically). Tests cover: (1) positive EP for each explicitly listed verb returning the correct status code, (2) negative path for invalid status codes returning 400, (3) boundary values at status code edges (100, 200, 299, 300, 400, 499, 500, 599), (4) decision table for weighted/comma-separated codes, and (5) exact status code pass-through to kill constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_all_verbs_accept_status_500
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, TRACE to /status/500
expected: All responses have status code exactly 500
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 -> all verbs -> status_code(500) -> 500 for each
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_verbs_accept_status_500():
    methods = [
        client.get, client.post, client.put,
        client.patch, client.delete, client.trace
    ]
    for method in methods:
        r = method('/status/500')
        assert r.status_code == 500

test_all_verbs_accept_status_500()

import json
client = app.test_client()

def test_status_code_406_content_type_json():
    r = client.get('/status/406')
    assert r.status_code == 406
    assert 'application/json' in r.headers.get('Content-Type', '')
    body = json.loads(r.data.decode('utf-8'))
    assert 'message' in body
    assert 'accept' in body
